thag12.1:1.2: Here master the virtue that in this world is well-mastered,
thag12.1:2.1: Wise, one should protect one’s virtue, aspiring to three pleasures:
thag12.1:2.3: the gaining of wealth, and—after death—rejoicing in heaven.
thag12.1:3.3: while the unvirtuous one, practicing evil,
thag12.1:4.1: The unvirtuous person gains disrepute & dishonor; the virtuous person, always,
thag12.1:5.1: Virtue is the beginning, the establishing,
thag12.1:5.2: the mother of what is fine, the foremost of all qualities:
thag12.1:7.4: Virtue: an astounding coat of mail.
thag12.1:8.2: Virtue: an unexcelled fragrance. Virtue: the highest fragrant ointment
thag12.1:8.4: by which one wafts this direction & that.
thag12.1:9.2: Virtue: the ultimate food for the journey.
thag12.1:9.4: by which one goes this direction & that.
thag12.1:10.3: he’s unhappy at heart: Everywhere the fool is unhappy at heart,
thag12.1:11.2: and after death, in heaven, is happy at heart:
thag12.1:11.3: Everywhere the enlightened one is happy at heart,
thag12.1:12.2: but one with discernment is the ultimate.
thag12.1:12.3: Among human beings & devas one conquers through virtue & discernment.
